chapters.title: The New Rules
chapters.sourcePressure: The source positions negotiation as a field-tested shift away from pressure-first bargaining toward rapport, tactical empathy, discovery, mirroring, getting to no, and triggering that's right.
chapters.coreMove: Replace winning the argument with making the other side feel safe enough to reveal what is really driving them.
chapters.commonMisread: Negotiation is just being nicer or more collaborative.

chapters.title: Be a Mirror
chapters.sourcePressure: The source defines mirroring as repeating the last or critical one to three words, slowing the exchange, allowing silence, and using a calm voice to test how solid the other side's position is.
chapters.coreMove: Echo the loaded few words and hold the silence so the other person expands the truth on their own.
chapters.commonMisread: Mirroring means parroting everything or pretending to agree.

chapters.title: Don't Feel Their Pain, Label It
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames tactical empathy as identifying and verbalizing the other side's perspective and emotions with recognition language such as it seems like and it sounds like.
chapters.coreMove: Name the pressure you hear without taking it on, so the other side can lower its guard.
chapters.commonMisread: Labeling means sympathizing, agreeing, or absorbing the other person's feelings.

chapters.title: Beware "Yes", Master "No"
chapters.sourcePressure: The source says yes can be a trap, while no-oriented questions preserve control, increase safety, and draw out deeper honesty.
chapters.coreMove: Invite a protected no so the other side can become honest without feeling cornered.
chapters.commonMisread: No is always progress or refusal should be celebrated for its own sake.

chapters.title: Trigger the Two Words That Immediately Transform Any Negotiation
chapters.sourcePressure: The source ties this chapter to that's right, summarizing, alignment, and permission to persuade after recognition and autonomy have been established.
chapters.coreMove: Summarize the other side so accurately that they feel understood enough to let persuasion begin.
chapters.commonMisread: The phrase that's right works like a verbal trick or compliment.

chapters.title: Bend Their Reality
chapters.sourcePressure: The source ties the chapter to fairness, loss aversion, anchoring, and perception, while warning against abstract behavioral-economics drift and careless manipulation.
chapters.coreMove: Frame the choice around the loss, fairness standard, or anchor that changes how the deal feels.
chapters.commonMisread: Perception-shaping is manipulation or a grab bag of cognitive biases.

chapters.title: Create the Illusion of Control
chapters.sourcePressure: The source ties this chapter to calibrated questions, collaboration, how questions, defusing conflict, and steering while preserving agency.
chapters.coreMove: Ask calibrated how and what questions that make the other side solve the path forward.
chapters.commonMisread: Open-ended questions are generally better than closed questions.

chapters.title: Guarantee Execution
chapters.sourcePressure: The source ties execution to implementation, liar detection, follow-through, and commitment, while warning that smooth verbal agreement is weaker than real readiness.
chapters.coreMove: Test agreement against implementation details until fake commitment has nowhere to hide.
chapters.commonMisread: A clear yes plus a deadline means the deal is secure.

chapters.title: Bargain Hard
chapters.sourcePressure: The source ties the chapter to price negotiation, haggling, non-round numbers, strategic umbrage, and resisting simple compromise after apparent agreement survives execution checks.
chapters.coreMove: Hold the price conversation firmly without collapsing into a split-the-difference compromise.
chapters.commonMisread: Bargaining hard means being aggressive, theatrical, or obsessed with exact formulas.

chapters.title: Find the Black Swan
chapters.sourcePressure: The source ties the close to unknown unknowns, hidden leverage, information asymmetry, and breakthrough facts that can overturn even strong bargaining logic.
chapters.coreMove: Keep probing past the visible deal until the hidden fact that changes leverage appears.
chapters.commonMisread: Every surprising detail is a black swan or intuition can replace disciplined discovery.
